title: How To: Use Action Items to Turn Coaching into Progress (A Guide for Employees)
summary: This guide walks through action items from the employee side of the table: where to find them, how to add and update your own, and how to close them out so your next 1:1 starts where the last one left off.
body_markdown:
A good 1:1 usually ends with a few next steps: follow up with a stalled deal, practice a new talk track, send your manager that forecast update. In Ambition, those next steps become action items, and they don't disappear when the meeting ends.


This guide walks through action items from the employee side of the table: where to find them, how to add and update your own, and how to close them out so your next 1:1 starts where the last one left off.


## 6 Steps to Turn Coaching into Progress


### **Step 1: Know where your action items live**


Action items come out of your coaching sessions, and you'll see them living in a few places:


- On your dashboard, in the Coaching tab
- Inside the session where the action item was created
- Under the Coaching History tab of any session


**Tip:** From your Homepage Coaching tab, select the ellipses next to an action item, then Details, to jump straight to the session it came from. It's a quick way to remember the context behind it.


### **Step 2: Add your own**


Action items aren't only something your manager hands you. If you leave a 1:1 with a next step in mind, add it yourself so it's written down in the same place as everything else.


- From a session page, click New Action Item in the Action Items section.
- Or go to Coach → Action Items → + Create Action Item.


Write the to-do, assign it, and add a due date and time if there's a deadline. The due date is optional, but it helps you and your manager agree on when it should be done.


### **Step 3: Check them off as you go**


When you finish something, open the action item and click the checkmark next to it. That's it. If you checked one off too soon, click the checkmark again to reopen it. Completed action items stay with the session they came from, so there's a record of what got done without cluttering your list of what's still open.


### **Step 4: Keep them up to date**


Plans change. If a to-do you created needs a new due date or clearer wording, update it: click the ellipses on the action item, choose Edit, make your changes, and click Save Action Item.


You can edit the action items you created. If one your manager created needs to change, mention it in your next session or ask them to update it.


### **Step 5: Bring them to your next 1:1**


Action items carry forward. If you're part of a coaching program, your next session shows them under View Action Items from Previous Program Check-in, so you and your manager can see what got done and what's still in progress, without anyone having to remember. In group sessions, action items work the same way. Participants can add them and complete the ones assigned to them, so the whole group can see follow-through.


### **Step 6: Choose which reminders you get**


Ambition can email you about coaching activity, including action items. To choose which emails you get:


- On your dashboard, click Edit Profile.
- Open the Notifications tab.
- Scroll to Coaching and use the Off/On toggle.


Emails from workflows your manager or admin set up can't be turned off. Only emails Ambition sends automatically can.


## **Why it matters**


A coaching conversation only changes results if something happens after it. Action items are where that happens. When you add, update, and close them out, your follow-through is visible to you and your manager, and every 1:1 can build on the last one instead of starting over.


Over time, your completed action items become a record of what you've worked on and how far you've come.


## **Try it this week**


After your next 1:1:


- Open your Coaching tab and find your open action items.
- Add one action item for a next step you agreed to in the meeting.
- Give it a due date.
- Check off anything you've already finished.
